predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Powys, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands

rulers.name: Bleddyn ap Cynfyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn
rulers.title: joint kings (Mathrafal line)

rulers.name: Cadwgan ap Bleddyn (with Iorwerth and Maredudd)

ledger.x: 540: the Gwertherion kingdom of Powys is on the map.
c. 550: Brochwel Ysgithrog 'may have moved the court from Caer Guricon to Pengwern' (Shrewsbury); the page lists him as c. 550 and gives no date for the move.
705: the Cliopatria shape loses its eastern edge toward Pengwern to Mercia.
By 717: the court moves west to Mathrafal in the Vyrnwy valley.
854: Cyngen dies and Rhodri Mawr of Gwynedd becomes king of Powys.
854: the Gwertherion line of Powys ends with Cyngen ap Cadell and the page's list passes to the dynasty of Manaw, Rhodri Mawr and his sons.
878: Powys has its own king again after Rhodri Mawr's death.
960: Powys is a separate shape again.
1039: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn heads the list of Welsh kings of Powys (1039-1063) and Cliopatria folds Powys into Gwynedd's shape from 1040 (10,634 km2).
1063: Powys passes to the Mathrafal line.
1063: Bleddyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn found the Mathrafal line, the page's third dynasty of Powys.
By 1086: the Normans take the east.
1099: the fighting over Powys ends with Cadwgan's return; the page gives 1098 for the Norman invasion and the following year for the return.

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith of Northumbria 'annihilated a combined force from the Welsh kingdoms of Powys and Rhôs'; Selyf Sarffgadau of Powys was killed.

wars.name: Battle of Maserfield
wars.outcome: Penda of Mercia defeated and killed Oswald of Northumbria on 5 August 642; Welsh poetry 'suggests that Penda fought in alliance with the men of Powys'.

wars.name: Offa's attack on Powys (Battle of Hereford)
Welsh revolt of 1094
wars.outcome: The rising of 1094 and the Norman invasion of 1098 end with Cadwgan reclaiming part of Powys in 1099 on homage to Earl Robert of Shrewsbury.

wars.name: Madog ap Maredudd and Owain Gwynedd
wars.outcome: 'In around 1150 Madog made an alliance with Ranulf de Gernon' before Owain Gwynedd defeated them near Ewloe and took Madog's lands in Iâl; in 1157 Madog backed Henry II's invasion of Gwynedd and 'regained many Welsh lands'.

certainty.note: Welsh kingdom frontiers are approximate throughout; the eastern edge against Mercia is the one line with physical markers (Wat's Dyke, Offa's Dyke), whose dating is disputed, and it is still drawn soft.
